summary: 1936 steel fire tower near Dillon, per a Florence Morning News item quoted on a lookout-history site; no source found on its later history or site today.

events.note: A Florence Morning News item dated March 11, 1936, as quoted on the lookout-history site, says a new steel tower was completed near Dillon. The year is taken from that item's date.
The same item names G.W. Byrd of Hamer as towerman and James L. Campbell as smokechaser, and says they were on duty.
Commission-wide: the SCFC closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993. This is not this tower's own closure date, and no source gives one.

evidence.supports: Dillon record: South Carolina Forestry Commission
Florence Morning News item of March 11, 1936: a new steel tower completed near Dillon
evidence.quote: Recently a new steel tower was completed near Dillon.

evidence.supports: Two men named for this tower: G.W. Byrd of Hamer as towerman, James L. Campbell of near Dillon as smokechaser
evidence.quote: G.W. Byrd of Hamer and James L. Campbell, of near Dillon, have been appointed towerman and 'smokechaser,' respectively, in connection with this tower.
They are now actively on duty.

evidence.supports: Lookout-history page gives only a satellite view for the site
SCFC closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Network eventually included more than 130 towers
evidence.quote: The tower network eventually included more than 130 towers and was used for 65 years to detect wildfires.

notes_for_editor: Only this record's lookout-history page and the statewide SCFC and Post and Courier pages were read, plus two searches. The 1936 date rests on a newspaper item quoted by the lookout site; the newspaper itself was not seen. The towerman and smokechaser names and the March 11, 1936 date were checked against the page on 2026-10-21 and match; the quote check on that date found every evidence quote. Two searches found no other Dillon County tower record. A 305-ft Dillon listing in search results looks like a communications tower and is not used. The Latta record in Dillon County is a different tower. The source-file coordinates (34.456, -79.3375) were not checked against a map. Before publishing any fate or site-today line, check SCFC records or the 1936 newspaper.
